items.stem: Why is validating the problem more important than perfecting the solution early on?

options.text: A great solution to a problem nobody has still fails
options.rationale: Correct: demand depends on a real, painful problem, not solution polish.
Solutions matter, but only for a validated problem.
Problems must be tested, not assumed.
Polish does not create demand that was never there.

items.explanation: Correct: demand depends on a real, painful problem, not solution polish.

items.stem: Which actions reflect a lean, experimental approach to a startup? (Select TWO)

options.text: Building a minimal version to test a key assumption
options.rationale: Correct: an MVP tests demand cheaply before full build-out.

options.text: Being willing to pivot when evidence contradicts the plan
options.rationale: Correct: responding to evidence is central to lean practice.

options.text: Building the complete product before talking to any customer
options.rationale: This risks large investment in something unwanted.

options.text: Ignoring metrics that contradict the founders' beliefs
options.rationale: Dismissing disconfirming evidence defeats the purpose of experiments.

items.explanation: Correct: an MVP tests demand cheaply before full build-out.

options.rationale: Correct: scaling an unproven product multiplies losses.

options.text: Evidence that the product is validated
A sound way to reduce risk
options.rationale: It increases burn and risk before fit is found.
